fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. David has just said he takes refuge in the LORD, and then he asks, “How then can you say to me: ‘Flee like a bird to your mountain!’” It's like telling a man who's already home to go look for a house. Pack up, fly off, find a mountain. David isn't taking that advice.

Yes, baker. The wicked set their arrow on the string “to shoot from the shadows at the upright in heart.” They're lining up the shot from the shadows, and I think that's a sneaky way to go about it. David puts it plainly in verse 2.

The poor and needy aren't named in this psalm, friend. The wicked set their arrow on the string to shoot at the upright in heart. That's a different crowd entirely, and caring about the poor is a fine instinct, but it'll lead you to the wrong box here. Keep the arrows pointed where David points them: at the upright in heart.

The widow and the orphan don't show up in this psalm. The wicked bend their bows and set their arrow on the string to shoot from the shadows at the upright in heart. It's easy to grab a familiar group when you're thinking about people who need protecting. Here David names someone else, so keep your eye on that phrase.

True, baker. David says, “His eyes are watching closely; they examine the sons of men.” That comes right after he says the LORD is on His heavenly throne. Watching closely and examining, that's what the verse says.

It's actually true. David says, “His eyes are watching closely; they examine the sons of men.” The LORD is on His heavenly throne, and His eyes watch closely. It's an easy one to doubt when the verse sounds so big.

Frogs and gnats aren't in this psalm. David says the LORD will rain down fiery coals and sulfur, and a scorching wind will be their portion. This is a heavy verse, so take your time with it. Take another look at verse 6.

Inheriting the whole earth isn't in this psalm. David's last line is, “The upright will see His face.” After all that tension, it's easy to expect something bigger. Look at the final sentence of verse 7 and you'll find what David says instead.
